title: eval-harness: integrate per-prompt metrics into CI gating and add regression check hooks
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Add per-prompt eval metrics and CI hooks to reduce prompt-set regressions; no breaking changes
description:
Motivation: We continue to see subtle regressions that only appear on a subset of prompts in our eval suite. The existing CI gating aggregates metrics across the whole prompt set which can mask per-prompt degradation. This PR adds per-prompt metric tracking and integrates per-prompt thresholds into CI gating so regressions can be detected and triaged earlier.

Changes in this PR: 1) Eval harness: extend metrics export to include per-prompt scores (accuracy, F1, BLEU where applicable, calibration/error rate) and delta vs baseline. 2) CI hooks: add a new GitHub Action that runs the eval harness on changes touching model adapters, prompt templates, or scoring logic and produces a per-prompt regression report artifact. 3) Quality gating: introduce configurable per-prompt thresholds and a severity mapping (warning/blocking) exposed via eval config. 4) Metrics integration: wire per-prompt outputs into our existing CI metrics dashboard (internal dashboard ID ENG-METRICS-12) and emit structured JSON artifacts for triage. 5) Tests and stability: add unit+integration tests and a small sample prompt set to exercise edge-cases (tokenization differences, sampling nondeterminism).

Checklist:
- [x] Add per-prompt metrics export from eval-harness
- [x] Implement GitHub Action and CI hook for per-prompt gating
- [x] Expose config for per-prompt thresholds and severity
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Update docs (docstring + docs/eval/ci.md)
- [x] Add migration for existing baseline artifacts

Compatibility/migration notes: The new per-prompt JSON artifacts are additive (old aggregated artifacts are still produced). CI config supports opt-in per-repo gating; org-level default is still aggregate gating for quick rollout. Baselines are generated automatically for the current main branch on merge; a follow-up job will backfill historical baselines for the last 30 days.

Why this matters: Several incidents in Q3 (see SUP-887) were caused by prompt-level regressions that slipped through aggregate SLOs. Per-prompt gating reduces mean time to detection and makes triage actionable by surfacing which prompt(s) regressed and the magnitude of the change.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on the GH Action security model (we use read-only model artifact keys and ephemeral credentials) and the threshold/config shape (eval/config/per_prompt_thresholds.yaml). The new tests intentionally exercise nondeterministic scoring by seeding RNG and checking statistical bounds instead of exact equality.

Files changed (high level): eval-harness/core/metrics.py, eval-harness/runner/ci_action.yml, ci/hooks/per_prompt_gate.py, eval-harness/configs/per_prompt_thresholds.yaml, docs/eval/ci.md, test/integration/test_per_prompt_metrics.py, scripts/migrate_baselines.py, tools/dashboard_publish.py

Migration steps (post-merge): run scripts/migrate_baselines.py --since=30d on a coordinator to generate baseline artifacts, and update repo-level .github/workflows/eval.yml to set per_prompt_gating: true when ready.

Jared Kim: Can we avoid writing secrets into GH logs? Please confirm action uses ephemeral creds and masks outputs.
Maya Thompson: Confirmed — action pulls ephemeral tokens from the coordinator role and we mask the artifact upload logs. Added explicit masking in runner.
Priya Anand: The per-prompt thresholds file looks heavy — can we support pattern-based defaults?
Maya Thompson: Added pattern support and defaults in per_prompt_thresholds.yaml (see commit 7d4e1b2). Also added docs describing override precedence.
Diego Fernandez: Test flakes observed locally for sampling-based metrics. Are we seeding RNGs?
Maya Thompson: Yes — tests use a fixed seed and statistical assertions; added additional retries in integration job to reduce CI flakiness.
Priya Anand: Approving pending green CI.
Jared Kim: Approved.
